Implementation Plan

The planning artefact for the `ai:unblock-closed` label-spoof finding is below.

Scope-mode: Hold Scope
Reuse-audit: extends handle_unblock_judge_project_hooks
Scope-mode justification: The finding concerns one branch of one function: `handle_unblock_judge_project_hooks` in `scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh` (lines 15765-15776). On the label alone, that branch writes `.status = "abandoned"` and closes the tracking issue through `PATCH issues/<n>`. The fix makes the branch require the authorization the unblock judge already writes. `scripts/unblock_judge.sh` (lines 590-622) posts a verdict comment on the item before it runs any operation. For a project, the item is the tracking issue itself, and the comment ends with `<!-- ai:unblock:v1 item=<tracking> stop=<id> fingerprint=<12hex> verdict=close round=<k> -->`. Only after that does `unblock_actions.py plan()` (verdict `close`, lines 300-306) add `ai:unblock-closed`. The judge, the actions planner and the ledger already produce everything needed, so none of them change. The complete fix (trusted marker, newest-marker rule, stop/state binding, close-retry for an already-abandoned project, tests, docs) is about 40 lines of bash/jq plus tests, adds no dependency and no external interface. Per the Boil the Lake rule and §6 (Security > Correctness & safety > Backward compatibility > Operational clarity > Performance > Speed), the complete option is chosen over a marker-presence-only check.

Planning ref: `git rev-parse HEAD` = `672e84b67c4731abf9a765fb5f05881485fb6bd6`, branch `claude/replace-claude-sessions-phase-7`, which matches the Integration branch metadata. The finding's location `scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:15765` matches this ref exactly: `if has_label "${TRACKING_LABELS}" "ai:unblock-closed"; then`.

## Automation / wiring (§20.E)
- New script: none. This only changes existing code: the existing poller function, tests, and docs.
- Scheduler entry point: unchanged. It runs on the existing per-project poll loop (`scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh`, around line 18619, `handle_unblock_judge_project_hooks || unblock_hook_rc=$?`), driven by `.github/workflows/internal-orchestrate-poll.yml` (cron `*/5`) → `.github/workflows/orchestrate_poll.yml`.
- New long-running supervisor: none needed.
- DB work: none.
- `docs/scripts-pending-removal.md` entry: none needed (no new script).

## 1. Files likely to change
- `scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh`: the `ai:unblock-closed` branch of `handle_unblock_judge_project_hooks` and its header comment (lines 15746-15761).
- `tests/test_unblock_scan.py`: new `_run_close_hook` harness and close-path tests, next to the existing `_run_fixup_hook` (line 212).
- `agents.md`: the "Unblock judge (Phase 7)" bullet, where it says "Label `ai:unblock-closed` marks an item the judge closed; on a tracking issue the poller sets state `abandoned` and closes the issue." Add the marker requirement.
- `README.md`: the `#unblock-judge` section, only if it repeats the label-only description. The implementer should search it for `ai:unblock-closed` and adjust only that sentence.
- `changelog.d/6314-unblock-close-requires-trusted-marker.md`: new fragment (CLAUDE.md §20 format). Assumption: this issue is #6314, per the planning memory record "Issue #6314 is clear"; the implementer should use the actual issue number.

## 2. Functions / modules to implement
In `handle_unblock_judge_project_hooks`, replace the unconditional branch with a guarded one. Pseudocode:

```
if has_label "${TRACKING_LABELS}" "ai:unblock-closed"; then
  close_reason=""
  unblock_trusted_login >/dev/null            # cached; at most one `user` GET per tick (already used by this function)
  login="${UNBLOCK_TRUSTED_LOGIN}"
  if [ -z "${login}" ]; then close_reason="login_unavailable"
  elif [ "${COMMENTS_FETCH_OK:-false}" != "true" ]; then close_reason="comments_unavailable"
  else
    close_marker="$(newest trusted ai:unblock:v1 marker for item=${TRACKING_NUM}, as JSON {stop, verdict} or empty)"
    if   [ -z "${close_marker}" ];               then close_reason="no_trusted_marker"
    elif [ verdict != "close" ];                 then close_reason="stale_marker"
    elif ! state_binding_ok;                     then close_reason="state_mismatch"
    fi
  fi
  if [ -n "${close_reason}" ]; then
    echo "UNBLOCK_PROJECT tracking_issue=${TRACKING_NUM} action=abandoned outcome=refused reason=${close_reason}"
    # fall through: the label has no effect; normal project processing continues
  else
    <existing abandon + PATCH close + log + return 10, unchanged>
  fi
fi
```

Marker selection, a single jq pass over the already-fetched `COMMENTS` with no new API call:
- Keep only comments where `(.user.login // "") == $login`.
- Take the last non-empty line of `.body`, after trimming CR and whitespace, matching `unblock_ledger.py parse_markers` ("the marker must be the last non-empty line").
- `capture` with the same shape as `unblock_ledger.MARKER_RE`: `^<!-- ai:unblock:v1 item=(?<item>[1-9][0-9]*) stop=(?<stop>[a-z-]+) fingerprint=[0-9a-f]{12} verdict=(?<verdict>[a-z_]+) round=[1-9][0-9]*(?: override=[a-z_]+)? -->$`.
- Keep only `.item == TRACKING_NUM`. Markers for child items, which the judge also posts on the tracking issue as "Unblock judge verdict on #<child>", are excluded.
- Choose the newest by the comment's integer `.id`, which GitHub assigns in increasing order, not by `created_at`. Per the stored lesson, whole-second timestamps do not order records reliably.

`state_binding_ok`, checked against the project's current state:
- `PROJECT_STATUS == "abandoned"`: OK. This lets a tick whose earlier `PATCH` close failed (`outcome=close_failed`) retry the close. Only this branch writes `abandoned`, and the marker check still applies.
- Else, marker `stop == "project-failed"`: OK only when `PROJECT_STATUS == "failed"`.
- Else: OK only when the label `ai:<stop>` is still present in `TRACKING_LABELS` (for example `ai:security-pass-failed` or `ai:validation-failed`). This mirrors how `unblock_judge.sh` (lines 428-436) derives a project's stop: a block label first, otherwise `project-failed`.
- Anything else (project resumed, `in_progress`, `security-pass`, `complete`, stop label cleared): refuse with `state_mismatch`.

Update the function's header comment to state that a close needs both the label and the newest trusted close marker bound to the current state, and that a refused label is logged and ignored.

## 3. Data structures affected
- No schema change. It reads the existing `COMMENTS` array, `COMMENTS_FETCH_OK`, `TRACKING_LABELS`, `PROJECT_STATUS` and `UNBLOCK_TRUSTED_LOGIN`.
- The project state is not mutated when the close is refused.
- No new state fields, labels or env vars.

## 4. API / interface changes
- No new GitHub API calls (§14). The only possible read is the existing per-tick cached `user` lookup in `unblock_trusted_login`; the comments are the paginated fetch at line 18466 the loop already makes.
- Log interface is additive, on the existing stable prefix `UNBLOCK_PROJECT`: `action=abandoned outcome=refused reason=login_unavailable|comments_unavailable|no_trusted_marker|stale_marker|state_mismatch`. The existing `outcome=closed|close_failed` lines are unchanged.
- The return-code contract is unchanged: 10 only on an authorized close, otherwise the function continues to the fix-up path and returns 0.

Failure modes:
- The judge posts its marker after the poller fetched comments but before it read labels (race). Symptom: one `reason=no_trusted_marker` line. Recovery: the next tick (5 minutes later) sees both and closes the project.
- The comments fetch fails (`COMMENTS_FETCH_OK=false`, `COMMENTS='[]'`). Symptom: `reason=comments_unavailable`. Recovery: the next tick. This fails closed.
- `GET user` fails. Symptom: `reason=login_unavailable`. Recovery: the next tick. This fails closed.
- A spoofed label stays on a live project. Symptom: one `refused` log line per tick, and the project otherwise proceeds normally. Recovery: a human removes the label. No automatic removal, see D3.
- An earlier authorized close failed at the `PATCH`. Symptom: state `abandoned`, issue still open. Recovery: the abandoned-state binding lets the next tick retry the close.

## Decisions
### D1 — Authorization source for abandoning a project
- Chosen: the newest pipeline-login-authored `<!-- ai:unblock:v1 item=<tracking> … verdict=close … -->` marker on the tracking issue (the last non-empty line of the comment), read from the already-fetched `COMMENTS`.
- Alternatives considered: (a) checking who added the label, via the issue timeline/events API; (b) a new dedicated close marker written by `unblock_actions.py`; (c) keeping the label as the trigger and only alerting.
- Why: the judge already writes this marker before it adds the label (`unblock_judge.sh` lines 611-615), it uses the same trust model as the ledger (`unblock_ledger.parse_markers`), and it needs no extra API call (§14). Option (a) adds a timeline read per tick. Option (b) duplicates an existing record. Option (c) leaves the exploit in place.

### D2 — Bind the marker to the current project state
- Chosen: require the newest such marker to be `verdict=close`, ordered by comment id. Its `stop` must match the current state (`project-failed` ⇔ status `failed`; otherwise `ai:<stop>` still on the tracking issue), except when the state is already `abandoned`, so a failed close can be retried.
- Alternatives considered: accept any trusted close marker that has ever existed; recompute the stop with `scripts/unblock_ledger.py stop`.
- Why: an old close verdict must not authorize closing a project that was later resumed by a human (`/judge_resume`, `/re-security-pass`, label removal).
